verification.notes: Section XI: Kirmira accosts Yudhishthira in the forest that is his dominion and declares his long-cherished desire to slay Bhima.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Kirmira-badha Parva, Section XI

verification.notes: Section XI: it is Vidura who narrates the destruction of Kirmira to Dhritarashtra at the latter's request.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Kirmira-badha Parva, Sections XI-XII

verification.notes: The Kirmira-badha Parva narrates the Rakshasa's encounter with the exiled Pandavas in the forest and his death at Bhima's hands.
Section XVII: Ravana seizes Vedavati by the hair; she cuts it off with her hand turned to a sword and enters the pyre, vowing to be born again to compass his destruction.
Section XVII: Vedavati declares, Narayana is my husband, and not any one else than that best of male beings, and carries on austerities for that end.
Section XVII: this is she that hath been born as the daughter of king Janaka, thy wife; Vedavati of the Krita age is reborn in the Maithila line of Janaka.
Section XVII: Vedavati names her sire Kucodwaja, a Brahmarshi of immeasurable energy, son unto Vrihaspati and like him in intelligence.
Section XVII of the Uttara Kanda tells Vedavati's story to Rama as the prior birth of Sita and the cause of Ravana's destruction.
Section LXXXV: when the ascetic names himself a Sudra called Sambuka, Rama takes out a sharp sword and chops off his head therewith.
Section LXXXV: the celestials shower flowers, saying that being slain by Rama this Sudra hath been able to attain to the abode of the celestials.
Section LXXXV narrates Sambuka's austerities, his admission that he is a Sudra seeking heaven in the body, and his beheading by Rama.
Section LXI: Richika refuses to sell his first-born and his wife her youngest, and the second son, Sunasepha, offers himself as the disposable one.
Section LXI: Ambarisha takes possession of Sunasepha by paying kotis of kine and heaps of jewels, and sets out with him placed on his car.
Section LXII: at Pushkara Sunasepha sees his maternal uncle Vicwamitra, flings himself into his lap and begs to be saved.
Bala Kanda LXI-LXII tell of Shunashepa's sale to Ambarisha as a sacrificial victim and his rescue by Vishwamitra.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana Parva, Section LIX

verification.notes: Section LIX: Kali, having possessed Nala, appears before Pushkara and urges, Come and play at dice with Nala, his brother.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana Parva, Section LXXVIII

verification.notes: Section LXXVIII: Nala says to his brother Pushkara, Let Damayanti and all else that I have be my stake, let thy kingdom be thy stake.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana Parva, Section LXXVIII

verification.notes: Section LXXVIII: in the rematch Nala offers Damayanti and all he has as stake against Pushkara's kingdom.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana Parva, Section LIX

verification.notes: Section LIX: Thus exhorted by Kali, Pushkara went to Nala and repeatedly said, Let us play together with dice.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana Parva, Sections LIX-LXXVIII

verification.notes: The Nalopakhyana tells how Pushkara, set on by Kali, wins Nala's kingdom at dice and years later loses it back in a single throw.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Ghatotkacha-badha Parva, Section CLXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXVIII: at Vasudeva's bidding Ghatotkacha abandons Karna, encounters Alayudha and slays him, beheading the cannibal.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Ghatotkacha-badha Parva, Section CLXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXVIII: Ghatotkacha encountered Alayudha, that prince of cannibals and brother of Vaka.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Ghatotkacha-badha Parva, Section CLXXVII

verification.notes: Section CLXXVII: Bhima rushes to rescue Ghatotkacha from Alayudha, and Alayudha abandons Ghatotkacha to proceed against Bhima himself.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Virata Parva, Pandava-pravesa Parva, Section XI

verification.notes: Section XI: Arjuna, his true form concealed in disguise, tells Virata, Know me to be Vrihannala, a son or daughter without father or mother.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Virata Parva, Pandava-pravesa Parva, Section XI

verification.notes: Section XI: Virata says, O Vrihannala, I give thee what thou desirest; instruct my daughter, and those like her, in dancing.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Virata Parva, Go-harana Parva, Section XXXVI

verification.notes: Section XXXVI: Uttara, told that Vrihannala was formerly the charioteer of Arjuna, sends his sister to fetch him from the dancing-hall to drive his car.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Virata Parva, Pandava-pravesa Parva, Section XI

verification.notes: Section XI narrates Arjuna's entry into Virata's court in the guise of Vrihannala, dancing-master to the women's apartments.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Indralokagamana Parva, Section XLII

verification.notes: Section XLII: the charioteer Matali, descending from the car, addresses Arjuna, saying, O lucky son of Sakra, Sakra himself wisheth to see thee.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Indralokagamana Parva, Section XLII

verification.notes: Section XLII of the Indralokagamana Parva brings Matali with Indra's celestial car to carry Arjuna to the world of the gods.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sabha Parva, Rajasuyarambha Parva, Section XVIII

verification.notes: Section XVIII: Krishna relates how the Rakshasi Jara, worshipped as Grihadevi in Vrihadratha's house, joined the fragmentary bodies into a living child.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Chaitraratha Parva, Section CLXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXVIII: Vasishtha's son Sakti curses Kalmashapada to become a Rakshasa subsisting on human flesh after the king whips him on the road.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Chaitraratha Parva, Section CLXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXVIII: Viswamitra, between whom and Vasishtha there was a dispute about the discipleship of Kalmashapada, approaches the place.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Chaitraratha Parva, Sections CLXXVIII-CLXXIX

verification.notes: These sections narrate Kalmashapada's curse into Rakshasa form, his devouring of Sakti, and his eventual ascent to heaven with Sakti.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XLIII

verification.notes: Section XLIII: Takshaka, having come out of the fruit as an insect, coiled round the king's neck, uttered a tremendous roar and bit that protector of the earth.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XLIII

verification.notes: Section XLIII: Parikshit himself places the insect on his neck, and Takshaka resuming his form bites him, fulfilling the Rishi's curse.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XLI

verification.notes: Section XLI: Takshaka, in the form of an old Brahmana, intercepts Kasyapa on the road as the latter hastens to cure Parikshit of his bite.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XLIII

verification.notes: Takshaka's killing of Parikshit in Section XLIII is the cause of the snake sacrifice that Parikshit's son Janamejaya undertakes.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Sections XLI-XLIII

verification.notes: Sections XLI-XLIII of the Astika Parva narrate Takshaka's bribing of Kasyapa and his slaying of king Parikshit.
